answer: Identity verification binds each claimed node to a Wesolowski VDF whose repeated modular squarings depend on the prior result, so a single proof chain has an unavoidable sequential time cost. GPUs may run separate clone chains concurrently, but cannot collapse one chain’s dependency sequence; multiplying identities therefore multiplies required work and hardware. The pearl in this lagoon is the measured delay: each computational thread must mature before its proof can be checked.
